article.headline: Hull break Brighton hearts late on as Oli McBurnie scores double to sink the Seagulls
article.description: Hull pounced at the death as Oli McBurnie struck twice in added time to snatch a 2-0 victory against high-flying Brighton at the MKM Stadium.
article.linkText: Hull break Brighton hearts late on as Oli McBurnie scores double to sink the Seagulls
article.story:
Hull pounced at the death as Oli McBurnie struck twice in added time to snatch a 2-0 victory against high-flying Brighton at the MKM Stadium.

The Tigers last tasted victory in late August against Coventry and have been held to a draw five times since, with all three of their losses coming away from home.

The MKM Stadium has become something of a fortress and Brighton had never enjoyed success on Humberside, but the Seagulls have been in immense form and arrived on Hull's doorstep second in the table and with the chance to close to within three points of leaders Arsenal.

Fabian Hurzeler's side were dominant but could not find a way through, thwarted on several occasions by Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis.

Their push for an eighth victory of the season was halted by Joao Costinha's dismissal a minute from time and, from there, the wheels came off.

McBurnie bundled home a fine Hull move two minutes into stoppage time and the Tigers were not done there as the striker buried his fourth goal in as many matches to lift his side up to 11th.

The momentum was with the hosts in the early minutes, as both McBurnie and Mohamed Belloumi looked poised to pose a threat.

Brighton then began to get the measure of their rivals and in the 16th minute Tzolakis was forced into a deft save as Diego Gómez picked up a dangerous Maxim De Cuyper cross and nearly made in 1-0.

Hull managed to force play up the other end and gained a useful free kick when Lewis Dunk collided with Tim Iroegbunam, but Regan Slater's resulting effort was headed away and the threat fizzled out.

The Tigers' next real opportunity came in the 31st minute when Mohamed-Ali Cho crossed to Matt Crooks, who just lacked the impetus to beat Bart Verbruggen.

There was then a quick counter attack at the other end of the pitch as Georginio Rutter had a chance, but Tzolakis blocked the shot with his legs.

As the first half drew to a close, Yasin Ayari hit the bar and Rutter got to the rebound, but Tzolakis produced another impressive save to ensure all was level going into the break -- with a late Brighton penalty shout dismissed as Pascal Gross felt he had been pushed in the goalmouth.

Hull went close to breaking the deadlock after 64 minutes when Belloumi darted through Brighton's defence but fired what was a valuable chance wide.

Just over 10 minutes later Tigers' hopes were raised again as substitute Sorba Thomas breathed new life into the game by hitting the woodwork, after which Hull looked dangerous again when Thomas pushed forward but was foiled by Dunk.

Costinha was shown a second yellow card for pushing Thomas and it was the break Hull needed. Regan Slater played in Lucas Gourna-Douath, who picked out McBurnie to prod into the bottom corner.

Before the dust had settled, the Tigers were on the move again with McBurnie the man at the forefront once more as he linked up with Belloumi to find space in front of an open goal in the 95th minute to seal the win.
